headline: P0086 (Family Practice, GA): 99215 share about 5x the complexity-adjusted expectation, concentrated on low-complexity patients with minor diagnoses
rationale: P0086 billed 32 of 356 claims (9.0%) as 99215. The expected share given patient complexity is 1.7%, and the risk-adjusted score is 3.93. The peer z-score is modest (0.53), so the concern comes from the provider's own patient mix, not from raw volume. The panel is mostly low complexity: 341 of 356 visits are for patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, and no 99215s were billed for patients with 4 or more conditions. In both low-complexity strata the provider's 99215 share is 8.2%, against 2.1% for all providers at 0 conditions and 3.4% at 1 condition. Those two strata account for 28 of the 32 99215s. In the sampled 99215 claims, many diagnoses are minor or self-limited: rash (C0042015, C0042140, C0042303), urinary tract infection (C0042010, C0042186, C0042238), unspecified abdominal pain (C0042080, C0042119, C0042266), upper respiratory infection (C0042225) and follow-up exams (C0042029, C0042329). Some patients appear more than once (C0042140/C0042186, C0042225/C0042303). The 2- and 3-condition strata show high shares too (27% and 25%), but on only 15 visits. Overall this pattern is consistent with upcoding rather than a sicker panel. However, the claim lists are samples and no clinical documentation is included, so the billed levels cannot be confirmed or refuted from this packet.
next_steps: Request medical records for the sampled 99215 claims on 0-condition patients (e.g., C0042010, C0042015, C0042029, C0042080, C0042225, C0042329) and check that MDM complexity or total time supports level 5.
Pull the full 99215 claim population rather than the sample to confirm the concentration on low-complexity patients and minor diagnoses.
Check whether 99215 is billed repeatedly for the same patients (e.g., P0086-N0086, P0086-N0011, P0086-N0111, P0086-N0145) and whether time-based billing or add-on services explain it.
Review the 99214 share (203 of 356 claims) on low-complexity patients, since comparison claims such as C0041999 (rash, no chronic conditions) suggest the whole distribution may be shifted upward.
Look at the 2-3 condition strata separately; their small visit counts (15 total) limit any conclusions.
